subject: NorthCoast AI - request: temporary latency variance & custom SLO
messages:
From: Evelyn Jones <evelyn.jones@northcoast.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@northcoast.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for model inference latency during peak window

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NorthCoast is close to committing to Redwood for our real-time assistant, but procurement and platform ops have a couple of asks before we sign: they want a documented SLA that covers our peak usage window (09:00-11:00 PT) with a p95 latency target of 100ms for the primary model and a clear fallback policy for capacity shortages.

Attached is our initial request (NorthCoast_SLA_Request_v1.pdf) and a pricing sheet. Two things to highlight:
- We expect sustained bursts up to 3x our baseline QPS for 6 weeks after go-live.
- Our security team will need evidence of KV cache behavior and any cold-start windows.

Can you loop in product/infra so we can understand whether Redwood can commit or propose an operational variance? Procurement would like an answer by end-of-week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Evelyn
Head of Platform Integrations
NorthCoast AI
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding NorthCoast's request. Key asks: 100ms p95 during 9-11am PT and clear fallback. They call out 3x burst for 6 weeks. Procurement wants decision EOW.

Immediate questions:
- Rishi/Karthik: feasible operationally? What would the cost/commit be to guarantee this for a strategic account?
- Aditya: product constraints (model variants, KV prewarm, routing policies) we should surface.

Thanks — Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA ask for model inference latency during peak window

Monica / all — quick technical read on feasibility and trade-offs. TL;DR: doable with a combination of Dedicated capacity + operational guardrails, but requires explicit limits and runbook windows.

Notes:
- Model choice: to hit ~100ms p95 at NorthCoast's projected QPS we should serve a quantized variant (x8 q4) of the chosen model and reserve a small Dedicated pool for peak hours (09:00-11:00 PT). Fully hosted elastic capacity will not give a predictable p95 without reserved capacity.
- KV cache warm: first-hour cold-start could add 50-150ms depending on prefix diversity. We can reduce this by pre-warming top 1000 keys via a prefetech job during the 30 minutes before peak.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a smaller variant (redwood-compat-small-q4) is possible, but outputs may be lower quality; need to document acceptable degradation.
- Cost: rough uplift estimate is 2.6x during peak window if we reserve capacity plus prewarm egress. Finance will want a committed monthly minimum for the dedicated pool.
- Monitoring: must enable per-route p95 dashboards and auto-notify SRE on >10% p95 drift.

Requested items from product/legal to finalize the variance:
1) A clear language block that calls out the peak window, reserved pool sizing, and the fallback model names.
2) A short tolerance table showing expected p50/p95 under normal and worst-case (cold-start) scenarios.
3) Ops runbook for cache warm and alert thresholds.

I can produce a draft runbook and sizing numbers if product confirms allowed model variants.

— Rishi
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: SLA ask for model inference latency during peak window

Thanks for the write-ups — appreciate the quick analysis. I’m ok to greenlight a conditional variance for NorthCoast with these product caveats:

Conditions for approval:
- Variance covers a fixed 90-day pilot window starting at go-live, with measurable checkpoints at day 14, 45, and 90.
- The SLA document must list the fallback model name and explicit quality disclaimers (we will not warrant semantic parity for fallback outputs).
- Prewarming/pre-fetch will be an ops task owned by SRE (Rishi) with a one-hour prewarm window; failure to complete prewarm that leads to p95 breaches will be treated as a non-conforming operational incident (not an SLA violation for Redwood).
- Any long-term committed p95 below our standard offering requires a commercial commitment (monthly reserved capacity fee).

Ask to product: Karthik, please enumerate allowed model toggles and any runbook snippets we can hand to the customer. Rishi, please draft the ops runbook and sizing numbers. Monica/Marissa, prepare a one-pager for Procurement with the conditional language.

If we can get those artifacts by Friday EOD, I’ll approve the variance and we’ll route to Legal for sign-off.

— Aditya Rao
VP Product | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Jones <evelyn.jones@northcoast.ai>, Procurement <procurement@northcoast.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: NorthCoast variance: conditional approval and next steps

Evelyn / team — thanks for the patience. Summary of internal decision and next steps:

What we can commit (conditional):
- 90-day pilot with a peak-window variance (09:00-11:00 PT) targeting p95=100ms for the primary quantized variant.
- Dedicated reserved pool during the peak window sized to handle the expected 3x burst.
- Pre-warm job to prime top-k KV keys 60 minutes prior to peak.
- Explicit fallback to redwood-compat-small-q4 with documented quality degradation.

What to expect in the SOW/Draft SLA:
- Checkpoints on day 14/45/90 with performance reports.
- A responsibility table that makes prewarm an SRE operational task; prewarm failure will be logged as an operational incident (we will not count it as an SLA breach).
- Committed monthly minimum for the reserved capacity will be included in the pricing appendix.

Attachments: we have attached an internal ops-impact matrix (ops-impact-matrix.csv) and the customer request you sent. Next steps:
1) Monica/Marissa will send the SOW draft + pricing appendix for Procurement by EOD Friday.
2) Rishi will upload the ops runbook and sizing numbers to the INF-1229 doc and share a short summary.
3) Once we have those artifacts, Aditya will sign off and we will route to Legal and DocuSign.

If this aligns, please confirm and we’ll proceed to draft.

Best — Monica Patel
